production.note: US model years 2020 to 2026. First: BMW NA's January 2019 release: 'Market Launch of the Z4 sDrive30i in March 2019. Z4 M40i to follow' and 'the 2020 BMW Z4 M40i Roadster, which will follow'. Last: BMW NA's release 'The BMW Z4 Final Edition' (26 November 2025; bmw-us-2026-z4-final-edition) has the spec header '2026 BMW Z4 Final Edition' and commemorates 'the end of production of the iconic 2-seat Roadster'. No page stating explicitly that no 2027 model was sold was opened.

body.note: Two-seat, two-door car with a soft top and no fixed-roof version (table: 2 seats, 2 doors), so 'Roadster' under the guide. C/D panel calls it a '2-door convertible'.

configuration.note: C/D panel: 'turbocharged and intercooled DOHC 24-valve inline-6'. BMW (bmw-us-2026-z4-final-edition): 'three-liter straight-six engine with TwinPower Turbo technology'.

aspiration.note: C/D panel: 'turbocharged and intercooled' (single turbocharger; BMW's 'TwinPower Turbo' is a brand name, not a turbo count).

fuel.note: Inferred from the panel's description ('direct fuel injection' gasoline inline-6).

transmission.note: 2026: 'Available with a 6-speed manual or 8-speed Steptronic transmission'. At launch the 8-speed Steptronic automatic was the only transmission (bmw-us-2020-z4-release: 'Transmission type | 8HP | automatic', 'standard eight-speed Steptronic Sport transmission'); the manual was added later in the run (the model year it arrived was not confirmed from an opened page).

powerHp.note: Quote: "Engine power | hp | 255 | 382" (Z4 sDrive30i | Z4 M40i); text: 'Drivers have 382 hp at their disposal'. Unchanged for 2026: "382 @ 5,800-6,500" (bmw-us-2026-z4-final-edition). C/D panel for 2023 (cd-2023-z4-m40i): "Power: 382 hp @ 6500 rpm".

weightLb.note: 2020 Z4 M40i with the 8-speed automatic, the only transmission that year; manufacturer step 1 for the launch (reference) year. Quote: "Curb weight | lbs. | 3,287 | 3,443" (Z4 sDrive30i | Z4 M40i). Other figures in discrepancies: BMW's 2026 figure '3,543 / 3,514 (6M)' and Car and Driver's 2023 road-test panel 3,636 lb.

discrepancies.reason: Model year and measurement: BMW's 2020 launch figure vs Car and Driver's road-test curb weight of a 2023 automatic test car ('Curb Weight: 3636 lb'). BMW's 2026 Final Edition release gives 'Curb weight (lbs) | 3,543 / 3,514 (6M)' (bmw-us-2026-z4-final-edition), i.e. 3,543 lb automatic and 3,514 lb manual for 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 3,443 lb: the reference year is the 2020 launch year (rating unchanged at 382 hp throughout) and a manufacturer figure exists for it (weight step 1).

reviewNotes: The task asked for this car to be built from the 2023 C/D panel, but BMW publishes curb weights (2020: 3,443 lb automatic; 2026: 3,543 lb automatic / 3,514 lb manual), so the guide's weight order puts the manufacturer figure first. A reviewer should confirm 3,443 lb (2020) is preferred over the panel's 3,636 lb (2023). The model year the 6-speed manual arrived was not confirmed.
